title: Sales and Negotiation Skills
subtitle: Sell by advising, win the next meeting and negotiate deals both sides keep
summary: Follow a needs-based sales process from prospecting to closing, handle objections honestly and negotiate a simple deal on interests, using a coffee exporter and an NGO payroll deal as running cases.
audience: Relationship managers, customer service officers and branch staff with sales targets in Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions. No prerequisites.
objectives: Follow a structured, needs-based sales process from prospecting to closing
Present bank products persuasively and handle common objections
Prepare for and conduct a simple negotiation using interest-based techniques
Sell within consumer protection rules: fair treatment, full disclosure and suitability

runningCase.name: Kaffa Ridge Coffee Export PLC and Tesfa Hiwot Development Association
runningCase.text: Dawit Mekonnen, a relationship manager at Bank A's Jimma branch, pursues two deals. Kaffa Ridge Coffee Export PLC, founded by Tigist Alemu, runs three washing stations, buys red cherry from about 2,400 smallholders, exported about Birr 410 million last year and pays 180 seasonal workers in cash. Its main bank provides a Birr 60 million pre-shipment facility, while Bank A holds only a Birr 1.5 million current account, and a fourth washing station is planned. Tesfa Hiwot Development Association, a Hawassa NGO with 420 staff and a monthly payroll of about Birr 9.66 million, wants to move its payroll. Modules 1 to 4 take Kaffa Ridge from prospect to proposal and follow-up; Module 5 negotiates the Tesfa Hiwot payroll deal, and both become the capstone role-plays.

modules.title: Selling in a bank
modules.summary: Understand why a bank sells by advising, where consumer protection draws the line, and how the sales cycle runs from first contact to follow-up.
objectives: Explain the difference between pushing a product and advising a customer
Apply the fair treatment, disclosure and suitability principles of consumer protection to everyday selling
Describe the seven stages of the bank sales cycle and measure conversion between them
Balance sales targets with conduct indicators such as dormancy and complaints

lessons.title: Selling versus advising
body: In a bank, the best salespeople rarely look like salespeople. They ask about the customer's business or household first, and only then suggest a product. Customers trust a bank with their money, so a sale that does not fit the customer damages the relationship and the bank's reputation long after the target has been counted.

Advising means starting from the customer's need and recommending what fits, even when that is a smaller or cheaper product. Pushing means starting from the product on this month's target list and looking for someone to take it. Both can close a deal today. Only advising brings the customer back, with referrals.

example.title: Two officers, one target
example.text: At a branch in Hawassa, two customer service officers each had to open 15 fixed-term deposits in a month. Lidya Tadesse persuaded a shoe trader, Ato Girma, to lock Birr 400,000 for a year. Two months later he needed the cash to pay a supplier, broke the deposit, lost most of the interest and complained. Biniam Kassa asked the same kind of trader how his cash moved during the week, opened a savings account with a debit card and a POS terminal instead, and booked a smaller deposit only for money the trader said he would not touch. Biniam's customer sent him three other traders from the same market.

lessons.tip: Before you name any product, be able to say in one sentence what problem it solves for this customer.

lessons.title: Why selling skills matter more now
body: Ethiopian banking has become far more competitive. Banks now set their own deposit and lending rates, the new Banking Business Proclamation opens the market to foreign banks, and mobile money and agent networks let customers move money without visiting a branch. A customer who is not well served can leave with a few taps.

In this market, staff who can find customers, understand them and keep them are worth more than any single product. Selling well is not about pressure; it is about being the person the customer calls first when they need something.

items.label: Deposits
items.text: Savings, current and fixed-term accounts, the bank's cheapest funding

items.label: Loans
items.text: Working capital, term loans and personal loans, subject to credit appraisal

items.label: Trade services
items.text: Export and import documents, FX retention accounts

items.label: Payroll
items.text: Salary accounts for a whole employer, one relationship, many customers

items.label: Digital
items.text: Mobile and internet banking, cards, POS and agents

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest Rates (As Amended), in force 9 January 2026
regulation.text: Each bank freely sets its deposit and lending rates. The rates must be approved in writing by the bank's board, based on explicit written criteria, and reported to the NBE. There is no longer a minimum savings rate, so banks compete on price and service, and staff must quote only the rates their bank has approved.

example.title: A salary customer who left quietly
example.text: Meron Alemayehu, a nurse in Adama, had her salary paid into a bank for six years but never spoke to anyone there. When a hospital colleague showed her a mobile app from another bank and a staff member called her to explain it, she moved her salary and savings the same week. Her old bank only noticed when the account went dormant.

lessons.title: Ethics and consumer protection limits
body: Consumer protection sets the outer line for every sales conversation. The NBE's financial consumer protection rules require fair treatment of customers, clear disclosure of costs, including the annual percentage rate on loans, a working complaints process and protection of customer data. NBE Proclamation No. 1359/2025 also gives the NBE consumer protection powers over banks.

In practice this means four habits: say only what is true, put every cost in writing, recommend only what suits the customer's needs and ability to pay, and never pressure a customer to sign today. If you are not sure whether a claim is accurate, do not make it.
points: No misleading claims: never call a product free if any fee applies
Disclose all costs before signing, including the APR for a loan
Suitability: match the product to the customer's needs and capacity
Respect the customer's right to say no and to complain

regulation.source: NBE financial consumer protection directive (reported as FCP/01/2020)
regulation.text: The directive is reported to require fair treatment of financial consumers, disclosure of costs including the annual percentage rate (APR), a complaints handling process and protection of customer data. Its detailed article numbers are not confirmed in this course, so follow your bank's compliance manual for the exact wording and forms.

scenario.title: The end-of-month target
scenario.situation: Selam Worku needs five more mobile banking activations to meet her monthly target. Ato Kebede, 72, visits the branch every Friday to withdraw cash. He has a basic phone and tells Selam he does not like using it for money.
scenario.question: What should Selam do?
options: Activate mobile banking on his account anyway, since it is free to him
Explain what mobile banking does, respect his choice, and look for customers who want it
Tell him the branch will soon stop cash withdrawals so he must activate
Activate it and keep the PIN herself so she can help him later
scenario.explain: Suitability and fair treatment mean selling only what the customer understands and wants. Activating without real consent creates a false target figure, and the other options are misleading or put his money at risk.

lessons.tip: If you would be uncomfortable reading your sales pitch aloud to your branch manager and to the NBE, change it.

lessons.title: The bank sales cycle
body: Every sale, from a youth savings account to a corporate payroll deal, passes through the same stages. Knowing where each prospect sits tells you what to do next and stops you from presenting before you understand the need.

Measure your own conversion from stage to stage. If many first meetings never become proposals, your discovery is weak. If proposals stall, look at pricing and objection handling. The numbers show where to practice.

items.label: Prospect
items.text: Build a list of people and firms with a likely need

items.label: Prepare
items.text: Research, plan the call, set the objective

items.label: Discover
items.text: Ask and listen until the need is clear

items.label: Present
items.text: Show how a solution meets that need

items.label: Handle objections
items.text: Listen, explore, answer honestly

items.label: Close
items.text: Agree the decision and the documents

items.label: Follow up
items.text: Deliver, check satisfaction, deepen

worked.title: Dawit's sales funnel last quarter

rows.label: Prospects needed for 6 deals at the same rates

worked.note: Dawit can reach his new target by contacting 60 prospects, or by raising one conversion rate. Moving meetings to proposals from 50% to 67% gives 12 proposals and about 5 deals from only 40 prospects.

lessons.title: Meet the running cases
body: This course follows Dawit Mekonnen, a relationship manager at Bank A's Jimma branch, through two deals. The first is a sales campaign for Kaffa Ridge Coffee Export PLC, a growing exporter that keeps only a small account with Bank A. The second, in the last module, is a negotiation for the payroll of Tesfa Hiwot Development Association, a local NGO in Hawassa.

Each module adds a step: researching Kaffa Ridge, discovering its needs, presenting a proposal and handling objections, and finally preparing and negotiating the Tesfa Hiwot deal. You will plan and role-play both in the capstone.

example.title: Kaffa Ridge Coffee Export PLC
example.text: Tigist Alemu founded Kaffa Ridge in 2016. It runs three washing stations in Jimma zone, buys red cherry from about 2,400 smallholders during the October to January harvest and exported coffee worth about Birr 410 million last year. It employs 35 permanent staff and about 180 seasonal workers, who are paid in cash. Its main bank provides a Birr 60 million pre-shipment facility, while Bank A holds a current account averaging Birr 1.5 million. Tigist plans a fourth washing station.

scenario.title: The goal of the first meeting
scenario.situation: Dawit has secured 45 minutes with Tigist Alemu and her finance manager, Samuel Haile. He knows Kaffa Ridge already has a main bank and a working pre-shipment facility.
scenario.question: What is the best objective for this first meeting?
options: Open three new accounts before he leaves
Present every Bank A product so they can choose
Understand how Kaffa Ridge's season and cash flow work, and agree a second meeting to discuss specific needs
Offer a lower interest rate than the main bank to win the facility
scenario.explain: A first meeting with an established company is for discovery and trust. Pushing for accounts or reciting the product list wastes the chance, and offering a price before knowing the need gives away value Dawit may not be authorized to give.

lessons.tip: Write the case details on one card and keep it with you. Good relationship managers remember the customer's numbers.

lessons.title: Targets, incentives and conduct
body: Targets are useful: they focus effort and reward people who build the business. The risk is that a target counts accounts opened, not customers served. Branch managers and staff should watch a few quality indicators next to the sales figures.

Accounts that go dormant within 90 days, products closed early, complaints about how a product was sold and requests for refunds are all signs of selling that did not fit. A good scorecard counts the active, profitable relationship, not the signature.
points: Dormancy within 90 days of opening
Early closure or early repayment penalties incurred
Complaints about how a product was sold
Share of customers holding two or more products after a year

worked.title: Two officers' quarter, quantity versus quality
worked.note: Lidya opened more accounts, but Biniam built more active relationships and created no conduct risk. A scorecard that counted only openings would reward the wrong behavior.

takeaways: In a bank, the best selling is advising: start from the customer's need, not the product list
Consumer protection requires fair treatment, full disclosure including APR, suitability and a working complaints process
Since NBE/INT/13/2026 banks set their own rates, so staff quote only board-approved prices and compete on service
Every sale passes through prospecting, preparation, discovery, presentation, objections, closing and follow-up
Measure conversion between stages and watch dormancy and complaints next to sales targets

quiz.q: What most clearly separates advising from pushing a product?
options: Advising starts from the customer's need and may recommend a smaller product
Advising uses a script
Advising never discusses price
Advising only happens with corporate customers
quiz.explain: Advising starts from the need, even when the right answer is a smaller sale.

quiz.q: Under NBE/INT/13/2026, who sets a bank's lending rates?
options: The NBE, through a fixed minimum
Each relationship manager for each customer
Each bank, with rates approved in writing by its board on explicit criteria
The Ministry of Finance
quiz.explain: Banks set rates freely, approved by the board on written criteria and reported to the NBE.

quiz.q: Which of these breaks consumer protection principles?
options: Giving a loan customer the APR in writing
Calling an account free when a monthly card fee applies
Telling a customer how to complain
Recommending a savings account instead of a deposit
quiz.explain: A free claim when a fee applies is misleading.

quiz.q: Dawit made 9 proposals from 18 meetings and closed 3. What is his proposal-to-close rate?
Which indicator best signals poor-quality selling?
options: High number of accounts opened
Many accounts dormant within 90 days
Customers asking for a second product
A long first meeting
quiz.explain: Early dormancy shows the product did not meet a real need.

quiz.q: At which stage should a relationship manager first suggest a specific product?
options: Prospecting
Preparation
After discovery, in the presentation
Before the first meeting, by email
quiz.explain: Products are presented only after needs are discovered.

modules.title: Prospecting and preparation
modules.summary: Build and rank a target list, use referrals and community networks respectfully, research a prospect and plan a call that earns the next meeting.
objectives: Build a target list from existing customers, value chains and local business activity, and score it
Use referrals and community networks such as iddir, equb, faith and business associations ethically
Research a prospect's business cycle before the first call
Write a call plan with an objective, questions, likely objections and a next step

lessons.title: Building a target list
body: Prospecting is the habit of always knowing who you will call next. The richest source is usually inside the bank: customers who hold only one product, borrowers whose suppliers and buyers bank elsewhere, and employers whose staff already have accounts with you. Outside the bank, look at industrial parks, new businesses in your branch area, cooperatives and exporters in local value chains.

A long list is not a plan. Score each prospect on a few criteria, rank them and work from the top. Review the list every month: some prospects move up when their situation changes, such as a new investment or a problem with their current bank.

items.label: Existing customers
items.text: Single-product holders, salary customers, depositors without loans

items.label: Value chains
items.text: Suppliers, buyers and transporters of current borrowers

items.label: Local business
items.text: New shops, workshops, hotels and clinics in the branch area

items.label: Exporters and cooperatives
items.text: Coffee, sesame, oilseeds, cooperatives and unions

items.label: Employers
items.text: Schools, hospitals, NGOs, factories for payroll

worked.title: Scoring three Jimma prospects (scores out of 5)

rows.label: Ranking
rows.value: Kaffa Ridge first, then Gibe Valley, then Sokoru

worked.note: Kaffa Ridge ranks first despite weaker access, because its need fit and value are high. Dawit's first task is to improve access by finding a warm introduction.

lessons.title: Referrals and the value chain
body: A referral from someone the prospect trusts is worth more than ten cold calls. Satisfied customers are usually happy to introduce you if you ask at the right moment: just after you have solved a problem for them, not on the day you open their account.

Follow the money through a customer's value chain. A borrower's trucking contractor, its raw material suppliers and its biggest buyers all have banking needs, and your customer can introduce you to them. Always thank the person who referred you and tell them how it went, without sharing the prospect's private details.

example.title: The truck owner's introduction
example.text: Abdi Mohammed, a Bank A borrower who runs eight trucks out of Jimma, carries coffee from washing stations to Addis Ababa. After Dawit helped him restructure his loan repayments around the harvest season, Dawit asked whether any of his clients might value a bank that understands the coffee calendar. Abdi named Kaffa Ridge and called Samuel Haile, its finance manager, that evening to say Dawit would be in touch.

lessons.tip: Ask for referrals by name: "Who among your suppliers would benefit from what we just did for you?" is easier to answer than "Do you know anyone?"

lessons.title: Community networks: iddir, equb, faith and business associations
body: Ethiopian communities are organized in strong networks. An iddir is a mutual support association that helps members with funeral costs. An equb is a rotating savings group in which members contribute regularly and take turns receiving the pot. Faith associations, mahbers and mosque or church committees, and business associations such as chambers of commerce, trade associations and cooperative unions, bring people together around shared purposes.

These groups often hold cash and their members have real banking needs, but they are built on trust. Approach them by offering value first: a financial literacy session, a group account that makes the treasurer's records clearer, or a safe way to keep the equb's money between rounds. Never use your access to members to pressure anyone, and never collect personal data without consent.

example.title: A financial literacy talk at an iddir meeting
example.text: Mekdes Fikre, a customer service officer in Adama, asked the chairperson of a neighborhood iddir whether she could give a 20-minute talk on household budgeting at the monthly meeting. She explained savings and how a group account would let the treasurer show members every deposit and withdrawal. The iddir opened a group account that month, and 38 members later opened personal savings accounts on their own initiative.

regulation.source: NBE financial consumer protection directive (reported as FCP/01/2020)
regulation.text: Consumer protection rules are reported to include protection of customer data. Collect contact details only from people who give them to you with their consent, use them only for the purpose explained, and never buy or accept member lists from a third party. Group accounts also need the normal customer identification and due diligence on the group and its signatories under the NBE's KYC rules.

scenario.title: The equb leader's list
scenario.situation: Ato Tesfaye leads an equb of 60 traders in Jimma's main market. He offers Dawit a list of all members' names and phone numbers if Bank A sponsors the equb's annual celebration.
scenario.question: What should Dawit do?
options: Accept the list and call every member this week
Decline the list, and instead ask to speak at a meeting so members who are interested can contact him
Accept the list but call only the members with the largest contributions
Pay for the celebration personally so the bank is not involved
scenario.explain: Members did not consent to their details being shared, so using the list would breach data protection and trust. Speaking at a meeting reaches the same people with their consent, and paying personally does not fix the consent problem.

lessons.title: Researching Kaffa Ridge before the first call
body: Preparation shows respect for the customer's time. Before calling Kaffa Ridge, Dawit gathers what he can: the coffee season, how exporters finance the harvest, the foreign exchange rules for exporters and what he can learn from Abdi about the company's operations.

His research gives him hypotheses, not conclusions. He suspects the company has a cash peak in December, pays seasonal workers in cash and may need more pre-shipment finance for the fourth washing station. The meeting will test these guesses with questions.

items.label: Aug to Sep
items.text: Prepare washing stations, hire seasonal workers, agree pre-shipment limits

items.label: Oct to Jan
items.text: Harvest: buy red cherry daily, cash peak, wages paid weekly

items.label: Jan to Apr
items.text: Process, grade and ship; export documents and contracts

items.label: Feb to Jun
items.text: Export proceeds arrive and repay the pre-shipment facility

items.label: Jun to Jul
items.text: Plan next season, invest in stations and equipment

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024, Foreign Exchange Directive, as amended by FXD/04/2026
regulation.text: Exporters must repatriate export proceeds within 90 days. They convert part of their earnings and may keep the rest in a foreign currency retention account; the July 2026 Monetary Policy Committee cut the surrender requirement on goods exports to 30%. FXD/04/2026 added forward contracts. An exporter's FX handling is therefore a real need a bank can serve.

scenario.title: What to bring to the first meeting
scenario.situation: Dawit has 45 minutes with Tigist and Samuel next Tuesday. He has a full Bank A product brochure, his research notes and a one-page summary of how Bank A handles exporters' FX retention accounts.
scenario.question: What should he bring and use?
options: The full brochure, to walk through every product page by page
His research notes to guide his questions, and the one-page FX summary only if FX handling comes up as a need
A pre-filled loan application for Birr 90 million
Nothing, so the meeting feels informal
scenario.explain: Research shapes good questions, and focused material is useful once a need is confirmed. A brochure walk-through or a pre-filled application assumes needs he has not yet discovered.

lessons.title: Planning the call
body: A call plan fits on one page. It states the objective of this meeting, what you already know, your hypotheses about needs, the questions you will ask, the objections you expect and the next step you will ask for at the end.
The objective should be specific and within the customer's power to agree today. "Win the account" is a hope. "Agree a site visit to the washing stations before the harvest begins" is an objective.

items.label: Objective
items.text: One specific result for this meeting

items.label: What we know
items.text: Business, season, current bank, people

items.label: Hypotheses
items.text: Needs we suspect but have not confirmed

items.label: Questions
items.text: Five to eight open questions in order

items.label: Likely objections
items.text: And honest answers

items.label: Next step
items.text: What we will ask the customer to agree

worked.title: Dawit's weighted pipeline for the quarter (annual revenue to Bank A, Birr)

rows.label: Kaffa Ridge: expected revenue 2,400,000 x 20% chance

worked.note: The weighted pipeline covers the goal by about 1.3 times. Moving Kaffa Ridge from 20% to 40% probability with a good first meeting would add Birr 480,000 on its own. All figures are illustrative.

lessons.title: Getting the first meeting
body: A warm introduction opens the door, but you still need a clear, short request. Introduce yourself and who referred you, give one reason the meeting is worth the customer's time, and ask for a specific time. Keep it under a minute on the phone.

Respect the customer's calendar. A coffee exporter in December is buying cherry from dawn to dusk; ask for a meeting before the harvest or after the busiest weeks. Avoid major holidays and fasting periods for long meetings, and be flexible about where to meet.
points: Name the person who referred you in the first sentence
Offer one concrete reason: a question about the coming season, not a product
Ask for 30 to 45 minutes at a specific time
Confirm by message and arrive on time

scenario.title: The busy finance manager
scenario.situation: Dawit calls Samuel Haile, mentioning Abdi's introduction. Samuel says politely: "We are happy with our bank, and the season starts soon."
scenario.question: What is Dawit's best response?
options: Say Bank A will beat their bank's interest rate
Thank him, say he is not asking them to move, and ask for 30 minutes before the season to learn how the company plans its cash peak
Ask to speak directly to Tigist instead
End the call and remove Kaffa Ridge from the list
scenario.explain: Acknowledging the existing relationship lowers resistance, and a short, specific, low-risk request is easy to accept. A price promise is unauthorized and premature, and going around Samuel would damage trust.

lessons.tip: Prospects rarely say yes to a product on a first call; they say yes to a short conversation with someone who seems to understand them.

takeaways: The best prospects are often already near the bank: single-product customers and the value chains of current borrowers
Score and rank prospects so effort goes where need, value and access are highest
Engage iddir, equb, faith and business associations by offering value first, with consent for any personal data
Research the customer's business cycle, then plan a call with a specific objective and next step
A weighted pipeline shows whether you can reach your target and which deal to advance next

quiz.q: What is an equb?
options: A funeral support association
A business chamber
A rotating savings group in which members take turns receiving the pot
A type of bank account
quiz.explain: An equb is a rotating savings group.

quiz.q: A prospect scores need fit 4, value 5, access 2 and risk 4, with weights 30%, 25%, 25% and 20%. Its weighted score is:
Which call objective is best?
options: Win the account
Make them like Bank A
Explain all our products
Agree a site visit to the washing stations before the harvest
quiz.explain: A good objective is specific and the customer can agree to it today.

quiz.q: A community leader offers you members' phone numbers. The right response is to:
options: Decline and reach members with their consent, for example by speaking at a meeting
Use it only for large savers
Accept if the bank pays a fee
Accept and delete it after a month
quiz.explain: Personal data needs the owner's consent.

quiz.q: Under FXD/01/2024, exporters must repatriate export proceeds within:
options: 30 days
60 days
90 days
180 days
quiz.explain: The directive sets a 90-day repatriation period.

quiz.q: A deal worth Birr 800,000 a year has a 25% chance of closing. Its weighted pipeline value is:

modules.title: Needs discovery
modules.summary: Use SPIN questions and active listening to uncover and size the customer's real pain points before presenting anything.
objectives: Ask situation, problem, implication and need-payoff questions in a natural sequence
Listen actively, paraphrase and read indirect signals common in Ethiopian business conversations
Turn a stated problem into a sized pain point with Birr figures
Summarize and prioritize needs and get the customer's agreement before presenting

lessons.title: Why questions beat pitches
body: Customers rarely buy a product; they buy relief from a problem or progress toward a goal. Until you know which problem matters most to this customer, any presentation is a guess. Good discovery means the customer talks for most of the meeting.

Questions also build trust. When a customer explains their business and hears you summarize it accurately, they feel understood, and that feeling, more than a brochure, earns the right to make a recommendation.

example.title: The pharmacy owner who wanted a loan
example.text: Rahel Desta owns two pharmacies in Bishoftu and asked her branch for a Birr 1.5 million loan to buy more stock. The relationship manager, Getachew Mulu, asked how quickly stock sold and how suppliers were paid. It emerged that her suppliers gave her 30 days, but two hospitals she supplied paid her after 75 days. Her real need was to collect faster and smooth the gap, so the final solution was a smaller overdraft of Birr 700,000 sized to the receivables, which cost her far less than the term loan she asked for.

lessons.tip: Aim to talk for no more than a third of a discovery meeting.

lessons.title: SPIN questioning
body: SPIN is a simple sequence for discovery questions. Situation questions collect facts. Problem questions find difficulties. Implication questions explore what those difficulties cost. Need-payoff questions let the customer describe the value of solving them.

Use few situation questions, because you should have learned most facts in preparation. Spend most of your time on problems and implications. When the customer explains the value of a solution in their own words, they are persuading themselves.

items.label: Situation
items.text: How many workers do the washing stations employ in the harvest, and how are they paid?

items.label: Problem
items.text: What difficulties does paying 180 people in cash create?

items.label: Implication
items.text: What did cash handling cost last season, in escorts, staff time and shortages?

items.label: Need-payoff
items.text: If wages went straight to workers' accounts or wallets, what would that mean for your supervisors?

example.title: Dawit's SPIN sequence at Kaffa Ridge
example.text: Dawit asked Tigist how she financed cherry purchases in December. She said the current Birr 60 million facility was usually enough. He asked what happened in the busiest week. Samuel admitted they had twice paused buying because the limit was full, and farmers sold to a competitor. Dawit asked what those lost purchases meant for the season's margin. Tigist estimated it at close to Birr 1 million. He then asked what an extra Birr 30 million of headroom would mean for the fourth station, and she said it would let her run it from the first week.

lessons.title: Active listening and indirect signals
body: Active listening means attending fully, letting the customer finish, paraphrasing what you heard and asking a follow-up before moving on. Take short notes, and say you are doing so; it shows you take the conversation seriously.

In many Ethiopian business settings people avoid a direct no, especially with a guest or a younger person. "We will think about it" or "Let us see" may be a polite refusal or a request for more time. Listen for hesitation, a change of subject or a glance at a senior colleague, and ask gently what would help them decide.

items.label: Attend
items.text: Phone away, eye contact, let them finish

items.label: Paraphrase
items.text: "So the limit fills in the second week of December?"

items.label: Probe
items.text: "What happens to the farmers when you pause buying?"

items.label: Check feeling
items.text: "It sounds as if that worries you most."

items.label: Summarize
items.text: Repeat the key needs before moving on

scenario.title: A polite "we will see"
scenario.situation: Halfway through the meeting, Dawit mentions Bank A could pay seasonal wages into workers' accounts. Samuel nods and says, "We will see," then looks at Tigist, who says nothing.
scenario.question: What should Dawit do?
options: Take it as a yes and move to the documents
Repeat the benefits more firmly
Ask openly what concerns they would need answered before considering it
Drop the subject for good
scenario.explain: "We will see" with a glance at the senior person may signal an unspoken concern. A gentle open question brings it out, for example whether workers without phones or IDs could still be paid. Pushing or assuming a yes ignores the signal.

lessons.title: Finding and sizing pain points
body: A problem the customer mentions becomes a priority when it has a size. Work with the customer to put Birr figures on it: direct costs, staff time, losses and missed opportunities. Use their numbers, not yours, and round sensibly.
Sizing does two things. It tells you which need to solve first, and it gives the customer a fair basis to compare the cost of your solution with the cost of doing nothing.

worked.title: Kaffa Ridge: cost of paying seasonal wages in cash (one season, Tigist's estimates)

rows.label: Cash wages: 180 workers x Birr 4,500 x 4 months
Cash transport and escort: 8 trips x Birr 12,000
Payroll staff time: 3 clerks x 12 days x Birr 900
As a share of wages paid

worked.note: Paying wages in cash costs Kaffa Ridge about Birr 173,400 a season before counting the safety risk to staff carrying cash. This is the benchmark for any payroll solution.

scenario.title: Which pain point first?
scenario.situation: Dawit has found three problems: the pre-shipment limit fills in December, costing Kaffa Ridge close to Birr 1 million in lost margin; cash wages cost about Birr 173,400 a season; and the current bank takes about a week to process export documents.
scenario.question: Which should Dawit lead with in his proposal?
options: The cash wages, because it is the easiest product to sell
The pre-shipment headroom, because it is the largest cost and matters most to Tigist, while making clear it depends on credit appraisal
The export documents, because it criticizes the current bank
None, he should wait for Kaffa Ridge to ask
scenario.explain: Lead with the need the customer values most, here the financing gap, while being honest that a facility needs credit approval. Payroll can be a quick first win alongside it, but it is not the main problem.

lessons.title: Exporter needs and the FX rules
body: An exporter's needs follow the foreign exchange rules. Proceeds must come home within 90 days, part is converted and part can be kept in a retention account, and since FXD/04/2026 banks can offer forward contracts. A relationship manager who explains these clearly is solving a real problem, not pushing a product.

Discovery questions here are practical: How long between shipment and payment? How do you use your retention balance? Do you import equipment or packaging? Have you lost value waiting for conversion? Each answer may point to a service, but the rules decide what is possible.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024, as amended by FXD/04/2026
regulation.text: Export proceeds must be repatriated within 90 days. Exporters keep part of their FX earnings in a retention account and convert the rest; the surrender requirement on goods exports was cut to 30% in July 2026. FXD/04/2026 introduced forward contracts and 100% retention for service exporters. Rates are freely negotiated between banks and customers.

example.title: Planning around the retention account
example.text: Samuel explained that Kaffa Ridge imports pulping machine spare parts each year and had once waited weeks for FX from another bank. Dawit noted that the company's own retention balance could pay for such imports, and that Bank A's trade desk could help plan the timing. Samuel said this would let him order parts before the harvest rather than during it.

scenario.title: Waiting for a better rate
scenario.situation: Tigist says she would like to hold a large shipment's proceeds abroad for 150 days, because she expects a better exchange rate later in the year.
scenario.question: What should Dawit say?
options: That Bank A can arrange the delay quietly
That proceeds must be repatriated within 90 days, and that Bank A can discuss options such as keeping the allowed share in a retention account or a forward contract
That the rules do not apply to coffee
Nothing, since FX is not his area
scenario.explain: The 90-day repatriation rule applies, so Dawit must say so plainly. He can still help by explaining the options the rules allow. Offering to bend the rule or staying silent are both wrong.

lessons.title: Confirming needs before you present
body: End discovery with a short summary: the needs you heard, in the customer's words, in their order of importance. Then ask whether you have understood correctly and whether anything is missing. This is the moment the customer agrees what the proposal must solve.

Separate what the customer said from what you inferred. An inferred need, such as a cash management account for the fourth station, should be raised as a question in the summary, not presented as fact.

left.title: Needs Tigist stated
items: Fourth washing station running from week one

right.title: Needs Dawit inferred, to confirm
items: Safer way to pay 180 seasonal workers
Planning help for the retention balance

lessons.tip: Ask "Have I missed anything that matters to you?" before you leave. The answer is often the most important need.

takeaways: Discovery comes before any presentation; the customer should talk most of the time
SPIN moves from situation to problem, implication and need-payoff, with most time on problems and implications
In Ethiopian business conversations an indirect answer may hide a concern; ask gently
Size pain points in Birr with the customer's own numbers
Exporters' needs are shaped by FXD/01/2024 and FXD/04/2026: 90-day repatriation, retention and forwards
Summarize needs, separate stated from inferred, and get agreement before presenting

quiz.q: "What did those paused purchases cost you in margin?" is which type of SPIN question?
options: Situation
Problem
Need-payoff
Implication
quiz.explain: It explores the consequence of a problem.

quiz.q: Why should situation questions be few?
options: Most facts should be learned in preparation, and too many bore the customer
They are rude
They are not allowed by consumer protection
They only suit retail customers
quiz.explain: Preparation covers most facts.

quiz.q: Wages of Birr 2,000,000 a season cost Birr 110,000 to pay in cash. The cost as a share of wages is:
A customer glances at her senior colleague and says "Let us see." The best reading is:
options: A firm yes
A possible unspoken concern or need for the senior person's view
A request for a lower price
A complaint
quiz.explain: Indirect answers often hide a concern.

quiz.q: Which statement about FX for goods exporters is correct?
options: Proceeds must be repatriated within 90 days and part may be kept in a retention account
Proceeds may stay abroad as long as they like
All proceeds must be converted the same day
Forward contracts are prohibited
quiz.explain: FXD/01/2024 sets 90 days and allows retention; FXD/04/2026 added forwards.

quiz.q: What should end a discovery meeting?
options: A signed application
A price quote
A summary of needs in priority order and the customer's confirmation
A list of all products
quiz.explain: Agreeing the needs sets up the proposal.

modules.title: Presenting, objections and closing
modules.summary: Present a tailored proposal in benefits, handle price objections with total cost and fair comparisons, close without pressure and follow up so the relationship grows.
objectives: Translate product features into benefits tied to a confirmed customer need
Handle price and other objections using listen, acknowledge, explore and respond
Compare Bank A's offer with a competitor's fairly and accurately
Choose a closing technique that fits the customer and record the deal and follow-up in the CRM

lessons.title: Features, advantages, benefits
body: A feature is what a product is or has. An advantage is what that feature does. A benefit is what the advantage means for this customer, tied to a need they confirmed. Customers decide on benefits, so every feature you mention should lead to one.
If you cannot link a feature to a need from discovery, leave it out. A short presentation of three relevant benefits beats a long tour of the product list.

parts.label: Feature: wages paid to workers' accounts or wallets
Advantage: no cash moved to the stations
Benefit: about Birr 173,400 a season saved and staff safer

visual.caption: Feature plus advantage only becomes a benefit when it answers a need the customer confirmed.

example.title: Same product, two presentations
example.text: Presenting payroll to a school in Jimma, one officer said: "Our payroll service has bulk upload and same-day credit." Another said: "You told me teachers queue for an hour on payday. With same-day credit to their accounts, they can use the app or an agent near home, and your bursar uploads one file instead of counting cash." The school chose the second officer's bank.

lessons.tip: After each benefit, check: "Would that help with what you described?"

lessons.title: Building Kaffa Ridge's proposal
body: Dawit's proposal follows the needs in Tigist's order. He leads with financing for the fourth station's season, explaining that Bank A's credit team will appraise the request and that he cannot promise approval or terms in advance. He then offers a payroll solution as a quick first step, trade services for export documents and help planning the retention balance.

Every cost goes in writing: the indicative interest rate and APR for any facility, account and transfer fees from Bank A's tariff, and what would change them. A proposal that hides a fee to look cheaper will be discovered, and the relationship will not survive it.

items.label: Pre-shipment finance
items.text: Request for Birr 90 million peak headroom, subject to credit appraisal

items.label: Seasonal payroll
items.text: Wages paid to 180 workers' accounts or wallets weekly

items.label: Export documents
items.text: Trade desk processing with an agreed turnaround

items.label: FX retention planning
items.text: Use retention balance for spare parts imports

items.label: Staff accounts
items.text: Salary accounts and cards for 35 permanent staff

regulation.source: NBE financial consumer protection directive (reported as FCP/01/2020)
regulation.text: Consumer protection rules are reported to require clear disclosure of all costs before a customer commits, including the APR on credit. A typical Ethiopian bank also requires that rates and fees be quoted from its board-approved pricing and published tariff, so any special pricing must be approved by the officer or committee with that authority before it is offered.

lessons.title: Handling price objections
body: An objection is information, not rejection. Use four steps: listen to the whole objection, acknowledge it honestly, explore what lies behind it, and respond with facts. "Your rate is higher" may mean the customer has not seen the total cost, has a real cheaper offer, or wants to test whether you will move.

Respond with the total cost of the relationship, not the rate alone. Include fees, processing time, the cost of problems your solution removes and the value of service. Then, if price is still the gap, escalate through your bank's pricing authority; never promise a rate you are not authorized to give.

items.label: Listen
items.text: Let the customer finish, without defending

items.label: Acknowledge
items.text: "Price matters, especially in the harvest."

items.label: Explore
items.text: "Is it the rate, the fees, or the total cost?"

items.label: Respond
items.text: Total cost, facts in writing, escalate if needed

worked.title: Kaffa Ridge: rate difference versus total value (one season, illustrative)

rows.label: Margin protected by extra headroom (Tigist's estimate)

worked.note: On the rate alone Bank A looks dearer, but the full package saves money and protects the season's margin. Rates here are illustrative; real figures come from Bank A's board-approved pricing and credit approval.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest Rates (As Amended)
regulation.text: Lending rates are set by each bank and approved in writing by its board on explicit written criteria. A relationship manager therefore negotiates within the approved pricing and the discretion delegated to them, and takes any request beyond it to the approving authority.

lessons.title: Comparing with competitors fairly
body: Customers will compare you with other banks, and they should. Compare fairly: use facts you can show, compare like with like, and talk about your strengths rather than the other bank's weaknesses. Never repeat rumors about another institution.

Fair comparison is also a consumer protection duty: a misleading comparison is a misleading sales practice. And it is good selling, because customers trust the person who gives them a balanced picture.
points: Compare the same product, amount and period
Include all fees and the APR, not only the headline rate
Say what the other bank does well if it is true
Never criticize a competitor's soundness or staff

scenario.title: The rumor about the other bank
scenario.situation: Tigist says her main bank's rate is 0.5 points lower. Dawit has heard gossip that the main bank is having liquidity problems and might cut limits.
scenario.question: What should Dawit say?
options: Warn Tigist that her bank may soon cut her limit
Acknowledge the lower rate, show the total cost and the benefits of Bank A's package, and say nothing about the rumor
Promise to match the rate immediately
Suggest she ask other customers about the main bank's problems
scenario.explain: Repeating an unverified rumor is misleading and could harm another institution and the customer's trust. Matching the rate without authority breaks pricing rules. Comparing total value on facts is fair and effective.

lessons.title: Closing techniques
body: Closing is simply asking for a decision once the customer has the information to make one. Good closes feel like a natural next step. A summary close restates the needs and the agreed solution. An alternative-choice close offers two acceptable options. A trial close checks readiness. A next-step close agrees what happens and when.

Pressure closes, such as false deadlines or saying an offer will vanish tomorrow when it will not, breach fair treatment and usually backfire. If the customer is not ready, agree a next step and a date.
points: Summary close: "We agreed three needs; this package covers them. Shall we start?"
Alternative choice: "Start with payroll this month, or together with the facility request?"
Trial close: "How does this fit what you had in mind?"
Next-step close: "Shall I bring the credit team to the stations next Thursday?"

scenario.title: Tigist is not ready on the facility
scenario.situation: Tigist likes the package but says moving the pre-shipment facility is a board decision, and the board meets in three weeks. She is happy to start payroll now.
scenario.question: Which close fits best?
options: Tell her the offer expires on Friday
Alternative choice: start payroll this month and prepare the facility papers for the board meeting
Insist on all products or none
Wait silently until she agrees to everything
scenario.explain: The alternative-choice close respects her board's process and secures a first win. A false deadline is a pressure tactic, and all-or-nothing risks losing the whole relationship.

lessons.title: Documentation, after-sales follow-up and CRM
body: A sale is complete only when the customer gets what was promised. Collect the documents the bank needs, including customer identification and due diligence on the company and its signatories, signed disclosures and account mandates, and check them before you leave the customer's office.

Record every meeting in the CRM: needs, what was offered, prices quoted and approvals obtained, objections and the agreed next step. Then follow up on a schedule. Most cross-selling opportunities appear in the first three months, when the customer sees whether you deliver.

items.label: Day 0
items.text: Documents checked, account live, thank-you message

items.label: Day 7
items.text: First payroll run checked with Samuel

items.label: Day 30
items.text: Review: problems, worker feedback, staff accounts

items.label: Day 90
items.text: Relationship review: facility request, trade services

example.title: The follow-up call that saved a deal
example.text: After the first payroll run, Dawit called Samuel and learned that 14 workers at the most remote station had no phone signal for wallets. He arranged for those workers to open basic accounts at a nearby agent instead. Samuel later told Tigist the problem had been fixed before he had to complain, and she invited Dawit to present the facility request to her board.

lessons.tip: If it is not in the CRM, it did not happen. Your successor and your manager should be able to pick up any relationship from your notes.

takeaways: Present benefits linked to confirmed needs; leave out features no one asked about
Put every cost in writing, including APR, and quote only board-approved prices and tariffs
Handle objections in four steps: listen, acknowledge, explore, respond
Answer price objections with total cost and escalate through pricing authority, never with unauthorized promises
Compare competitors fairly and never repeat rumors
Close without pressure, then document, record in the CRM and follow up at day 7, 30 and 90

quiz.q: "Workers are paid without cash at the stations, saving about Birr 173,400 a season" is a:
options: Feature
Benefit
Advantage
Objection
quiz.explain: It states the value to this customer.

quiz.q: A facility of Birr 40 million is used for 6 months. The rate difference between two banks is 0.5 points. The extra interest is:
A customer asks for a rate below your delegated pricing. You should:
options: Explain the total value and take the request to the approving authority
Agree to keep the deal
Quote it and correct it later
Refuse to discuss price
quiz.explain: Rates are board-approved; escalate beyond your discretion.

quiz.q: Which is a pressure close that breaks fair treatment?
options: Summary close
Next-step close
Saying an offer ends tomorrow when it does not
Alternative-choice close
quiz.explain: A false deadline is misleading.

quiz.q: What is the first step in handling an objection?
options: Respond with facts
Listen to the whole objection
Offer a discount
Escalate
quiz.explain: Listening comes first.

quiz.q: Which belongs in a CRM record after a meeting?
options: Needs, offer, prices quoted, approvals, objections and the next step
Only the deal size
Nothing until the deal closes
The customer's personal opinions about competitors
quiz.explain: A full record lets anyone continue the relationship.

modules.title: Negotiation basics and the capstone
modules.summary: Negotiate on interests rather than positions, know your BATNA and walk-away point, trade concessions, respect Ethiopian business norms and run the capstone role-plays.
objectives: Distinguish positions from interests and find options that serve both sides
Work out each side's BATNA, reservation point and the zone of possible agreement
Plan and trade concessions within the bank's pricing authority and related party rules
Adapt negotiation style to Ethiopian business norms
Prepare and perform the capstone sales call and payroll negotiation against the rubric

lessons.title: Positions versus interests
body: A position is what someone says they want. An interest is why they want it. Principled negotiation focuses on interests, because two parties with opposite positions often have interests that can both be met.

When the other side states a position, ask why it matters, what problem it solves and what would happen without it. Then look for options that meet their interest at a lower cost to you, and explain your own interests openly.

left.title: Tesfa Hiwot's positions
items: A dedicated desk at the branch

right.title: Interests behind them
items: Keep admin costs low for donors
Salaries paid on time, problems fixed fast

example.title: Tesfa Hiwot Development Association
example.text: Tesfa Hiwot is a local NGO in Hawassa running health and education projects, with 420 staff and a monthly net payroll of about Birr 9.66 million. Donor project funds in its operating accounts average about Birr 18 million. Its current bank charges Birr 10 per salary transfer, and payroll is often a day late. Executive Director Almaz Getachew and finance head Yared Abebe have asked Bank A for a proposal, starting with the four positions on the left.

lessons.title: BATNA, reservation point and ZOPA
body: Your BATNA is your best alternative to a negotiated agreement: what you will do if this deal fails. Your reservation point is the worst deal you will accept, set before you start. The zone of possible agreement, or ZOPA, is the range where both sides' reservation points overlap.

Estimate the other side's BATNA too. If Tesfa Hiwot's alternative is to stay with a bank that charges fees and pays late, Bank A does not need to give everything away to win. If Bank A's alternative is a pipeline of other payroll prospects, Dawit can walk away from a deal that loses money.

items.label: Our BATNA
items.text: Other payroll prospects in the pipeline

items.label: Their BATNA
items.text: Stay with current bank: fees and late payroll

items.label: Our reservation point
items.text: Approved pricing floor, no interest-free lending

items.label: Their reservation point
items.text: Total cost no higher than today, with better service

items.label: ZOPA
items.text: Fee relief for moving all accounts, standard-priced advances

worked.title: Tesfa Hiwot: what the current bank costs the NGO each year
worked.note: The NGO's BATNA costs it Birr 50,400 a year plus late salaries and staff frustration. Any Bank A offer that is cheaper and more reliable is inside its zone of agreement.

lessons.title: Preparing the Tesfa Hiwot negotiation
body: Preparation decides most negotiations. Dawit estimates the deal's value to Bank A, the cost of each concession, what he is authorized to give and what needs approval. He lists the NGO's interests and the options that might meet them, and decides his opening offer, his target and his walk-away point.

He also checks the rules. Any fee waiver must be approved by the officer or committee with pricing authority under Bank A's tariff, and any rate must come from board-approved pricing. He gets the approval range before the meeting, so he can trade without pausing to call the branch.

worked.title: Value of the Tesfa Hiwot relationship to Bank A (annual, illustrative)

rows.label: Operating account balance Birr 18,000,000 x 7% net value of funds
Staff account balances 420 x Birr 6,000 x 7%
Transfer fees at standard tariff 5,040 x Birr 10
Cost of waiving all transfer fees
Cost of a dedicated desk (share of one officer)

worked.note: The balances, not the fees, carry the value. Dawit can afford fee relief if it secures the operating accounts, but not interest-free loans, which would breach approved pricing and suitability. The 7% net value of funds is an illustrative assumption.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest Rates (As Amended), and the bank's tariff and pricing authority
regulation.text: Rates must come from the bank's board-approved pricing, set on explicit written criteria and reported to the NBE. In a typical Ethiopian bank, fees come from a published tariff, and only named officers or committees may waive or reduce them, within set limits. A negotiator agrees only what is inside that authority.

lessons.title: Making and trading concessions
body: Never give a concession; trade it. Every "yes" from you should be linked to something you value: "If you move the operating accounts as well as payroll, then we can waive transfer fees for two years." Start with small concessions, make each one smaller than the last, and keep a written record of what was offered.

Package the issues. Negotiating fees, advances, service and timing together lets each side give on what matters less to it. Avoid splitting the difference on a single number; it rewards whoever opened most extremely.
points: Use "if you ... then we ..." for every concession
Make concessions smaller as you go, to signal you are near your limit
Trade low-cost items you can give, such as service standards and timing
Put the agreed package in writing at the end

scenario.title: "Waive all fees, then we will talk"
scenario.situation: At the start of the meeting, Yared says Tesfa Hiwot will only discuss the rest of the proposal if Bank A first agrees to waive all fees, permanently.
scenario.question: What should Dawit do?
options: Agree, since fees are only Birr 50,400
Acknowledge that cost matters, explore why, and offer fee relief linked to moving the operating accounts as part of a package
Refuse to discuss fees at all
Promise a permanent waiver without approval and fix it later
scenario.explain: Giving the waiver up front loses the main bargaining tool for the operating accounts, which carry most of the value. Refusing ignores a real interest, and promising without approval breaks pricing authority.

lessons.title: Cultural norms in Ethiopian business negotiation
body: Negotiation in Ethiopia usually rests on relationships. Customers want to know and trust the person before they commit, so time spent over coffee, asking about family and the organization's work, is not wasted. Respect for seniority matters: greet and address the most senior person first, and let them speak.

Decisions are often made by consensus, a board or elders, so expect pauses and second meetings. A direct "no" is rare; disagreement may come indirectly or through a trusted intermediary. Avoid causing anyone to lose face in front of colleagues, and plan around religious holidays and fasting periods.

items.label: Relationship first
items.text: Trust before terms; coffee and conversation count

items.label: Respect seniority
items.text: Address the senior person first and let them lead

items.label: Allow time
items.text: Boards and elders decide; expect a second meeting

items.label: Save face
items.text: Disagree privately and politely, never publicly

items.label: Mind the calendar
items.text: Holidays, fasting and harvest seasons

example.title: The second meeting
example.text: At the first meeting, Almaz Getachew listened, served coffee, asked about Dawit's family and said little about terms. Dawit did not push. A week later she invited him back with Yared and two board members, and said the board wanted to hear how Bank A would handle donor audit statements. The real negotiation started only then.

scenario.title: Silence from the senior person
scenario.situation: Dawit makes his package offer. Yared responds positively, but Almaz is quiet and says, "We will discuss it among ourselves."
scenario.question: What is Dawit's best next move?
options: Ask Almaz directly in front of her team why she does not like it
Thank them, offer to answer any question the board has, and agree a date to meet again
Lower the offer immediately to win her over
Press Yared to sign today since he seems positive
scenario.explain: Her response signals a consensus decision, not necessarily rejection. Respecting the process and agreeing a next step keeps the deal alive. Cutting the price unasked or pressing a junior colleague would weaken Dawit's position and trust.

lessons.title: When the other side is connected to the bank
body: Sometimes the other side has a link to the bank, such as a director, a significant shareholder or a senior executive, or a close relative of one. The NBE's related party rules require dealings with related parties to be at arm's length, that is, on the same terms as with anyone else.

If you learn of such a link, do not offer special terms, and tell compliance or your manager so the bank can decide whether the related party rules apply. A good deal on normal terms protects both the bank and the customer.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/88/2024, Related Party Transactions
regulation.text: Transactions with related parties must be on arm's length terms. Exposure to a single related party is limited to 15% and to all related parties together to 35%, and transactions above Birr 15 million require board approval. Whether a counterparty is a related party is decided under the directive's definitions, so refer any doubt to compliance.

scenario.title: A board member's request
scenario.situation: A Tesfa Hiwot board member mentions that her brother is a director of Bank A and asks Dawit to give the NGO a rate below Bank A's approved pricing on a Birr 5 million vehicle loan, "as family."
scenario.question: What should Dawit do?
options: Give the lower rate, since the director will approve it anyway
Explain that Bank A offers the same terms to everyone, quote standard pricing and report the link to compliance
Decline to work with the NGO
Ask the director to call the credit team directly
scenario.explain: Related party dealings must be at arm's length, and compliance decides whether the rules apply. Special pricing or a director's call would break that principle; refusing the NGO is unnecessary.

lessons.title: Capstone: the role-plays and the rubric
body: The capstone has two role-plays. In the first you plan and conduct the Kaffa Ridge sales call: a short call plan, a discovery conversation using SPIN, a tailored proposal and handling at least two objections. In the second you negotiate the Tesfa Hiwot payroll deal, using your preparation sheet, BATNA and concession plan.

Assessors score each role-play on a rubric, and the course ends with a knowledge test. The suggested pass mark for every course in the programme is 70%. Ethics carries real weight: a misleading claim or an unauthorized promise lowers the score however good the outcome looks.

items.label: Prepare
items.text: Call plan for Kaffa Ridge, preparation sheet for Tesfa Hiwot

items.label: Sales call
items.text: Discover, present, handle objections, close a next step

items.label: Negotiate
items.text: Interests, options, concessions, written package

items.label: Debrief
items.text: Assessor and peer feedback against the rubric

items.label: Test
items.text: Knowledge test on all five modules

worked.title: Scoring one learner's role-plays (scores out of 5)
worked.note: The learner passes, with discovery and negotiation as the areas to practice. The weights shown are an example; the trainer sets the final rubric.

lessons.tip: In the role-play, ask for a specific next step at the end of each conversation. Assessors look for it.

takeaways: Negotiate on interests, not positions, and look for options that serve both sides
Know both sides' BATNA and set your reservation point before you start
Trade every concession with "if you ... then we ...", inside your pricing authority
Relationship, seniority, consensus and saving face shape Ethiopian business negotiations
Related party dealings must be at arm's length under SBB/88/2024; refer any link to compliance
The capstone combines a sales call and a negotiation, scored on a rubric with a 70% pass mark

quiz.q: "We need zero fees" is best described as:
options: An interest
A BATNA
A position
A reservation point
quiz.explain: It is what they say they want; the interest is why.

quiz.q: What is a BATNA?
options: Your best alternative if no agreement is reached
The lowest price you will offer
The first offer in a negotiation
A bank tariff item
quiz.explain: It is the best alternative to a negotiated agreement.

quiz.q: An NGO pays 380 salaries a month at Birr 10 each. Its annual transfer fees are:
options: Birr 3,800
Birr 38,000
Birr 4,560
Birr 45,600

quiz.q: Which phrasing trades rather than gives a concession?
options: "We can waive the fees."
"If you move the operating accounts, then we can waive transfer fees for two years."
"Let us split the difference."
"Fees are not negotiable."
quiz.explain: It links the concession to something the bank values.

quiz.q: Under SBB/88/2024, related party transactions above Birr 15 million require:
options: Branch manager approval
NBE approval in advance
Board approval
No approval
quiz.explain: The directive requires board approval above Birr 15 million.

quiz.q: In the capstone rubric example, which result passes?
quiz.explain: The suggested pass mark is 70%.

exam.q: A relationship manager opened 50 accounts in a quarter; 20 were dormant after 90 days and there were 3 sales complaints. Another opened 36, with 4 dormant and no complaints. Which statement is best?
options: The first officer performed better because volume matters most
The second officer built more active relationships with less conduct risk
Both performed the same
Dormancy is the customer's responsibility
exam.explain: 30 active versus 32 active, and no complaints: quality beats volume.

exam.q: Under NBE/INT/13/2026, a customer asks why Bank A's savings rate differs from another bank's. The accurate answer is:
options: The NBE sets one rate for all banks
Rates depend on the branch manager
The minimum savings rate is the same everywhere
Each bank sets its own rates, approved by its board on written criteria
exam.explain: Banks set rates freely; there is no minimum savings rate.

exam.q: Dawit closed 5 deals from 50 prospects. His goal is 8 deals next quarter at the same conversion. How many prospects does he need?
A prospect scores need fit 3, value 5, access 4 and risk 2, with weights 30%, 25%, 25% and 20%. What is its score?
A women entrepreneurs' association invites you to speak. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Collect all attendees' phone numbers from the organizer beforehand
Sign members up for loans on the spot
Offer practical financial content and let interested members contact you
Offer gifts in exchange for account openings
exam.explain: Offer value first and respect consent.

exam.q: Tigist wants to keep a shipment's proceeds abroad for 120 days. Under FXD/01/2024, what applies?
options: No limit applies to coffee
Proceeds must be repatriated within 90 days
Proceeds must be repatriated within 30 days
Only the surrendered share must be repatriated

exam.q: Which is a need-payoff question for Kaffa Ridge?
options: How many washing stations do you run?
What problems does cash payroll cause?
What did cash handling cost last season?
If wages went straight to workers' accounts, what would that free your supervisors to do?
exam.explain: Need-payoff questions let the customer state the value of a solution.

exam.q: A school pays 60 teachers Birr 9,000 a month for 10 months in cash. Cash handling costs Birr 27,000 a year. What share of wages is that?
Which statement is a benefit rather than a feature?
options: Bulk salary upload
Same-day credit
Teachers no longer queue on payday and the bursar stops counting cash
Mobile app with transfer function
exam.explain: A benefit states value tied to the customer's need.

exam.q: A Birr 50 million facility is used for 4 months. Bank A's rate is 0.6 points higher than a competitor's. The extra interest is:
options: Birr 75,000

exam.q: Continuing: Bank A's package also removes cash payroll costs of Birr 140,000. What is the customer's net position with Bank A?
options: Better by Birr 40,000
Worse by Birr 40,000
Better by Birr 240,000
Equal

exam.q: A customer says a competitor is cheaper. Which response best follows the four-step method?
options: "Their bank is in trouble."
"I will match it now."
"Our rates are fixed, take it or leave it."
"I understand price matters. Is it the rate, the fees or the total cost? Let me show the full comparison."
exam.explain: Acknowledge, explore, then respond with facts.

exam.q: Which disclosure is required before a customer signs a loan, under consumer protection principles?
options: Only the monthly installment
All costs, including the APR, in writing
Only the interest rate
Nothing until the first payment

exam.q: A customer must consult her board in three weeks before moving a facility. Which close is most appropriate?
options: A false deadline
All or nothing
An alternative choice: start payroll now and prepare board papers
A summary close followed by silence until she signs
exam.explain: It respects her process and secures a first step.

exam.q: Tesfa Hiwot's current bank charges Birr 10 per transfer for 420 staff, and payroll is often late. What is the NGO's BATNA?
options: Staying with its current bank at Birr 50,400 a year with late payrolls
Bank A's offer
Paying staff in cash
Zero fees
exam.explain: The BATNA is its best alternative if no deal is reached with Bank A.

exam.q: In the Tesfa Hiwot deal, most of the value to Bank A comes from:
options: Transfer fees
The dedicated desk
Salary advance interest
Operating and staff account balances
exam.explain: Balances worth about Birr 1.44 million dwarf Birr 50,400 of fees.

exam.q: A fee waiver costs Bank A Birr 50,400 a year on a relationship worth Birr 1,486,800. What share of value is it?
The NGO asks for interest-free salary advances for all staff. The best negotiating response is to:
options: Agree, to win the deal
Refuse to discuss staff needs
Explore the interest, such as emergencies, and offer a standard-priced, quick-approval advance or other support within approved pricing
Promise to ask the board for a 0% rate
exam.explain: Meet the interest within board-approved pricing and suitability.

exam.q: During a negotiation, the executive director goes quiet and says, "We will discuss it among ourselves." What does this most likely mean in an Ethiopian business setting?
options: A consensus decision is needed; agree a next step
A firm rejection
A request for a bribe
A sign to lower the price immediately
exam.explain: It signals a collective decision, not necessarily refusal.

exam.q: A director's relative asks for below-tariff pricing for a Birr 20 million facility. Under SBB/88/2024, what applies if they are a related party?
options: Special pricing is allowed for family
Only branch approval
The NBE sets the rate
Arm's length terms and board approval because it exceeds Birr 15 million
exam.explain: Related party dealings must be at arm's length, with board approval above Birr 15 million.
